::: {.callout-important}
## Warning — Uncalibrated Model
This is the **Phase 3** version of the report. Base geometry still comes from
OSM (with imagery-based corrections to the deck lane count, merge-junction
type, and pier/bay structure) and baseline demand remains entirely
**hypothetical** (engineering guesswork, not field data). From this version
on, per the project's Hard Rule 5, every reported number is a **mean ± 95%
confidence interval over at least 10 seeds** — but since only the S0 (do-
nothing) scenario exists so far, this report contains **no scenario
comparison** (do-nothing vs. improvement options); that comes in Phase 4. What
is here is how sensitive the existing condition (S0) itself is to demand
level.
:::

## 1. Purpose of this version

Per the project roadmap (`CLAUDE.md`), Phase 1's goal was a **complete,
end-to-end** pipeline — from raw OSM data to a published report — even with raw
geometry and demand. Phase 2 brought the critical geometry (deck lane count,
merge-junction type, pier/bay structure) and fleet composition closer to
imagery evidence / engineering judgment on that same pipeline. Phase 3 (this
version) adds the **multi-λ × multi-seed** infrastructure required by the
project's Hard Rule 5 and measures how sensitive the existing condition (S0)
is to demand level — the statistical prerequisite for a meaningful scenario
comparison in Phase 4.

## 2. Network construction and grade-separation check

The network was built from OpenStreetMap (Overpass API, bbox around the Seyedi
under-bridge intersection) using `netconvert`. Separation between the elevated
bridge deck (Imam Reza Highway, `bridge=yes layer=1`) and the at-grade network
below (Seyedi road / Shahid Soleimani Blvd) was **visually inspected and
confirmed** (@fig-layer-check) — per `CLAUDE.md` this is the single most
critical failure point for this model.

![Visual grade-separation check: red = bridge deck (z>0), blue = at-grade network (z=0). The deck passes over the ground network with no connection.](../outputs/figures/network_layer_check_zoom.png){#fig-layer-check width=85%}

## 3. Demand: the jtrrouter method

Per `CLAUDE.md`'s methodology justification, for a single intersection, entry
volume per approach + turning ratios is far less data-hungry than a full OD
matrix. Demand in this version is entirely hypothetical (see
`config/assumptions.yml`, sections `demand_baseline_phase1` and
`traffic_control.turn_ratio_baseline`):

| Approach | Hypothetical entry volume (veh/h) |
|---|---|
| West (bridge deck) | 800 |
| East (bridge deck) | 800 |
| North (Seyedi road) | 500 |
| South (Shahid Soleimani Blvd) | 500 |

## 4. Geometric fidelity and fleet composition (Phase 2)

**Imagery-based geometric corrections** (applied to the plain-XML via
`src/02_patch_geometry.py`, per Hard Rule 2 — no manual netedit editing):

- **Bridge deck lane count:** OSM recorded 2 lanes per direction; a closer
  review of `2025_zoom.png` (clearly three rows of vehicles) showed 3 lanes
  with high confidence — corrected. See
  `config/assumptions.yml -> bridge_geometry.deck_lanes_per_direction`.
- **Merge-junction type under the bridge:** 9 merge junctions (2 in / 1 out) in
  the weaving area were changed from netconvert's default `priority` to
  `zipper` — to represent the real "first-come-first-served" behavior in the
  absence of channelization or signals (see
  `traffic_control.weave_merge_junction_model`).

**Key geometric finding — the bridge's 7-bay pier structure:** a close visual
inspection by the user of `2012.png` (when the bridge structure was still bare
and the piers fully visible) showed that, along the bridge's east-west axis,
the space under the deck is divided into 7 bays: 3 on the west + 1 center bay
+ 3 on the east (@fig-sketch). Of the 3 bays on each side, only the one
**adjacent to the center** is open to traffic and is where vehicles actually
pass/turn; the two outer bays on each side are completely closed and are part
of the bridge's structural body (not usable open space), and the center bay is
currently kept deliberately closed. This means the weaving area under the
bridge is not, contrary to the Phase-0 assumption, one continuous open
plaza — it is exactly **two discrete choke points** (the west open bay and the
east open bay) separated by a closed structural section; the observed
roundabout-like weaving behavior arises from vehicles circulating between
exactly these two choke points. **Scenario implication:** opening the center
bay (subject to a structural engineer confirming load-bearing capacity — outside
this traffic study's scope) is an explicit Phase-4 option that would open a
third through-corridor under the bridge. See
`config/assumptions.yml -> bridge_geometry.span_structure`.

![Updated geometric sketch with the bridge's real 7-bay pier structure (green label = open bay, red label = closed bay)](../outputs/figures/seyedi_sketch.png){#fig-sketch width=90%}

**Fleet composition and behavior** (`config/vtypes.yml`, all flagged
`sensitivity: true` in `assumptions.yml`):

```{python}
#| label: tbl-fleet
#| tbl-cap: "Hypothetical fleet composition (engineering judgment — calibration priority #1)"
import yaml
from IPython.display import Markdown
vcfg = yaml.safe_load(open("../config/vtypes.yml", encoding="utf-8"))
names = {"passenger": "Passenger car", "motorcycle": "Motorcycle", "taxi": "Taxi",
         "pickup": "Pickup", "bus": "Bus", "truck_light": "Light truck"}
rows = [{"Category": names[k], "Share": f"{v['share']*100:.0f}%"} for k, v in vcfg["fleet_composition"].items()]
import pandas as pd
Markdown(pd.DataFrame(rows).to_markdown(index=False))
```

The **sublane** model was enabled (`--lateral-resolution 0.8`) to represent
motorcycle filtering between lanes; `tau`, `minGap`, `sigma`, `impatience`,
`jmIgnoreFoeProb`, and `lcAssertive` were all set more aggressively than SUMO
defaults across classes (most aggressive for motorcycles).

::: {.callout-warning}
## Notable qualitative finding
S0 runs with `collision.action=warn` (vehicles are not removed after a
collision) so collisions are logged rather than truncating the simulation.
The full collision-vs-demand trend (mean over 10 seeds per level) is in
Section 6 ("Sensitivity to demand level"); here it suffices to say it grows
far faster than delay does as demand rises — a qualitative signal of high
conflict density absent channelization, consistent with this study's core
motivation. Surrogate safety measures (TTC/DRAC/PET) will be reported
statistically in Phase 4.
:::

## 5. Baseline run result (λ=1.0, mean of 10 seeds)

```{python}
#| label: tbl-kpi
#| tbl-cap: "KPI summary by approach — scenario S0, lambda=1.0, mean of 10 seeds"
import pandas as pd
df = pd.read_csv("../outputs/tables/s0_kpi_summary.csv")
df.columns = ["Approach", "N vehicles", "Mean duration (s)",
              "Mean time loss (s)", "Mean waiting (s)", "Mean route length (m)"]
from IPython.display import Markdown
Markdown(df.round(2).to_markdown(index=False))
```

![Mean time loss by approach (lambda=1.0, mean of 10 seeds)](../outputs/figures/s0_timeloss_by_approach.png){#fig-timeloss width=85%}

Across all 50 runs (5 lambda levels x 10 seeds), every generated vehicle
entered the network and completed its trip — a basic health signal for
network connectivity and routing even at the highest demand level (lambda=1.4).

## 6. Sensitivity to demand level (lambda)

Per the project's Hard Rule 5 and Phase 3, scenario S0 was run at 5 demand
levels (lambda in {0.6, 0.8, 1.0, 1.2, 1.4}) x 10 independent seeds (used for
both jtrrouter's stochastic turn assignment and sumo's own random behavior) —
50 runs total. @fig-sensitivity shows mean time loss and collision count with
95% confidence intervals.

![S0 sensitivity to lambda — mean ± 95% CI over 10 seeds](../outputs/figures/s0_sensitivity_lambda.png){#fig-sensitivity width=95%}

```{python}
#| label: tbl-lambda
#| tbl-cap: "Mean ± 95% CI per lambda level (10 seeds)"
dfl = pd.read_csv("../outputs/tables/s0_lambda_summary.csv")
dfl = dfl[dfl["metric"].isin(["mean_timeloss_s", "n_collisions"])]
metric_en = {"mean_timeloss_s": "Mean time loss (s)", "n_collisions": "Mean collision count"}
dfl["metric"] = dfl["metric"].map(metric_en)
dfl = dfl[["lambda", "metric", "mean", "ci95_lo", "ci95_hi"]].round(2)
dfl.columns = ["lambda", "Metric", "Mean", "CI95 low", "CI95 high"]
Markdown(dfl.to_markdown(index=False))
```

**Key finding:** mean time loss rises at a fairly steady slope, from 17.8 s
(lambda=0.6) to 27.3 s (lambda=1.4) — about a 54% increase. The recorded
collision count, however, grows **far faster and non-linearly**: from a mean
of 1.3 at lambda=0.6 to 101.5 at lambda=1.4 (roughly 80x). This asymmetry —
linear delay growth versus exponential-looking safety degradation — is exactly
what would be expected for an unchannelized weaving area with two discrete
choke points (Section 4): as demand rises, safe merging opportunities shrink
faster than average delay grows.

::: {.callout-warning}
## Methodology note — confidence interval on a collision count
The `n_collisions` confidence interval uses the standard t-based method
(suited to continuous data) and goes negative at low lambda (meaningless for a
count) — a statistical artifact, not a claim of negative collisions. A proper
Phase-4 estimate needs a count model (Poisson / negative binomial). Still, the
**mean trend** (exponential-looking growth with lambda) is clearly visible and
significant across the 50-run dataset.
:::

## 7. Limitations of this version

- Ramp turning radii still come directly from OSM / visual estimation; no
  field measurement or precisely scaled imagery backs them yet (bridge bay
  widths are likewise schematic — see Section 4).
- Baseline demand (volume per approach) and turning ratios are entirely
  hypothetical; what this phase calls "sensitivity" is scaling that same
  hypothetical demand, not replacing it with field evidence — still pending
  (`CLAUDE.md` §5).
- Fleet shares (especially the 30% motorcycle share), left-turn share, and the
  behavioral aggressiveness multiplier (tau) are registered in
  `assumptions.yml` as future global-sensitivity factors but have not been
  tested yet; "turning radius" as a sensitivity factor requires rebuilding
  network geometry and was deferred to Phase 4 (alongside building scenarios
  S1-S5).
- Only one scenario (S0) has been built; **no scenario comparison can be drawn
  from this report** — per the project's Hard Rule 5. What was reported is
  S0's *within-scenario* sensitivity to demand, not a ranking of options.
- The collision-count confidence interval uses a method suited to continuous
  data (see the warning above); to be corrected in Phase 4.
- The Persian report uses the Vazirmatn font with a full RTL layout
  (xepersian); final visual polish still happens in Phase 5.
